Looking at the graph, the curve crosses the x-axis at four points within [-6, 6]:

- At x = -3 (curve descends from above, crossing downward)
- At x = -1 (curve rises from the minimum near x = -2, crossing upward)
- At x = 1 (curve descends from the local maximum at (0, 1), crossing downward)
- At x = 3 (curve rises from the minimum near x = 2, crossing upward)

Between these crossings the function dips below the axis (minima near x = -2 and x = 2) and rises above it (local maximum at x = 0), confirming each crossing is a sign change. Outside x = ±3 the curve rises steeply and stays positive, so there are no additional zeros in [-6, 6].

Thus the distinct real zeros are x = -3, -1, 1, 3.

\boxed{4}
